title: feat(state): local client credential cutover (R0 PR1b)

commit.messageHeadline: feat(state): local client credential cutover (R0 PR1b)
fix(test): use local credentials in rebased restart fixtures
test(state): reconcile credential fixtures with current main
fix(gateway): preserve dispatch errors when failure recording conflicts
fix(state): retain private-store attribution through rebase
fix(ci): preserve explicit singleton worker limits
fix(state): preserve credential restore and owner contracts
fix(state): inspect installed PostgreSQL schema before capture
fix(state): preserve updater custody in PostgreSQL inspection
fix(state): qualify schema SQL and isolate bounded test assets
test(worker): report relocated watcher startup failures
fix(build): retain fs-safe worker entry effects
test(gateway): await node result acknowledgements before teardown
test(worktrees): enable diagnostics for eviction log capture
fix(mantis): retain prepared native assets for offline candidates
fix(state): validate native credential receipts consistently
test(build): capture worker source across bundling stages
test: keep declaration fixture writes inside owned paths
test(codex): await rollout watcher delivery
test: pin late lease proof to acquisition path
test: preserve current completion notices after restart
test: align credential capture attribution metadata
refactor(infra): retain shared socket transport for credential cutover

Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR moves client identities, cached tokens, and native socket secrets into a separately versioned local SQLite store. **Example:** A CLI installation uses PostgreSQL for Gateway state. - **Before:** Client identity and token access depends on the selected shared-state database. - **After:** Private client credentials use <resolved-client-root>/client/credentials.sqlite at local schema version 1. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The inspected repairs are coherent with no new confirmed defect; final native authority evidence remains absent, and review coverage does not certify every changed fixture. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Private client credential access remains coupled to the Gateway's selected shared-state database. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction and merged prerequisite approve separating local secrets while preserving identity bytes, pairing authority, and rollback behavior. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** Keep open: this maintainer-approved cutover remains necessary, the two latest findings are addressed, and the explicit landing pause still applies. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: provide the scheduled signed real-Mac client.credentials trace showing allowed access and rejection of foreign UID, unowned-root, and closed or replaced owner requests before credential I/O or disclosure, including closure while work waits. Recorded PostgreSQL, updater, and native harness results support their declared scenarios but explicitly exclude this app run; redact secrets, IPs, and non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body, then request a new review with `@clawsweeper re-review`. The PR author or someone with repository write access can request it. - [ ] **Resolve security review attention item** - No concrete bypass was established, but the new credential-disclosure boundary still needs its scheduled authority proof. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk** - Final-effect authorization for native credential disclosure after owner closure or replacement remains unverified. - [ ] **Complete next step** - Resolve the conflicts GitHub reports for the reviewed head and validate the affected integration changes. ## Findings None. ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The scheduled signed-app credential authority scenario remains unshown, and the archive regression has no recorded failing base run.
Agent review details ### How this fits together CLI and Apple clients submit bounded credential operations to the active app or an exclusive offline owner; migration and restore owners preserve the shared/local binding. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[CLI and Apple clients] --> B[Credential routing] B --> C[Authenticated app control] B --> D[Exclusive offline custody] C --> E[Local credential SQLite] D --> E F[Doctor and updater] --> E F --> G[Shared state migration] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Complete the approved single-owner cutover with exact migration and restore binding, preserving the documented rollback contract. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? This is an approved architectural cutover; current-main source confirms the shared-storage coupling, and no runtime reproduction was attempted during this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The inspected implementation uses one local credential owner and existing migration, backup, and capture coordinators; the two requested repairs fit those owners without introducing competing state. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [0a0d88df543a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0a0d88df543a9d36c4708f93c56d995da769050c). ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Complete the scheduled native verification (recommended)** Establish allowed and forbidden final credential effects through the signed app before lifting the landing pause. 2. **Retain the landing pause** Keep this PR open while the native proof coordinator completes the scheduled verification. ### Provenance checked - `Cross-runtime identity persistence` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (98410d986eee7ce7cff8e8466c6d5f9314ae784b: The earlier migration established one SQLite identity owner and preserved key material across Node and Apple clients.) - `Native adoption of CLI-written identities` keeps the original intent (374007083a52e51d9b4e1d386d61fde585b0544f: Native startup needed to adopt valid canonical identities during shared-state migration without rotating trust or accepting corrupt rows.) - `Legacy import and rollback` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174294: The approved cutover requires copy-only independent sources, durable consumed-import claims, and rebuilding stale local state from authoritative rollback images.) - `Migration publication attribution` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174360: The existing capture coordinator attributes committed migration changes while preserving exact rollback and rejecting foreign writes.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security Needs attention: No concrete bypass was established, but the new credential-disclosure boundary still needs its scheduled authority proof. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Archive-alias finding addressed:** Backup capture records the canonical shared source identity separately from lexical archive paths, and restore uses that captured identity rather than resolving a potentially vanished source alias. ([`src/infra/client-credential-restore.ts:192`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98/src/infra/client-credential-restore.ts#L192), [01695d5df1dc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98)) - **Restore regression coverage:** The restore suite exercises aliased sources after both original paths disappear, exact identity preservation, mismatched capture rejection, and incomplete-target cleanup; the body explicitly reports no pre-fix runtime failure run. ([`src/infra/client-credential-restore.test.ts:244`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98/src/infra/client-credential-restore.test.ts#L244), [01695d5df1dc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98)) - **Planner finding addressed:** The retained first-sign-in expectation now selects vitest.gateway-server-isolated.config.ts, consistent with its current Gateway-server routing. ([`test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.test.ts:860`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98/test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.test.ts#L860), [01695d5df1dc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98)) - **Native authority boundary:** App control checks peer UID and request authentication; credential execution checks configured roots and retains a closeable custody object through each operation. ([`apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceCredentialAccess.swift:303`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98/apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceCredentialAccess.swift#L303), [01695d5df1dc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98)) - **Approved compatibility contract:** The merged prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174294 records published v2026.10.4 and beta capture/restore experiments, copy-only independent native sources, and the accepted loss of credentials issued between upgrade and rollback; this PR retains that contract. Public docs: [`docs/install/updating.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating). ([`docs/install/updating.md:109`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating), [4706053bc398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4706053bc398d6ccf519a4d21fb1e9ed1cecb31d)) - **Explicit landing pause and conflicts:** The full body and latest maintainer comment explicitly leave signed real-Mac proof pending and say not to merge; REST also reports mergeable=false and mergeable_state=dirty for the reviewed head. ([01695d5df1dc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01695d5df1dc12530bbaf4d9a32af5569ad2ec98)) Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Raw commit 98410d986eee7ce7cff8e8466c6d5f9314ae784b adds apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceIdentitySQLiteStore.swift:6 relative to its recorded parents. This identifies author metadata, not feature responsibility or a PR merger. Members: - `superseded`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174485 - The body identifies this closed, unmerged predecessor as replaced by the current cutover. - `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174294 - The merged preparatory owner intentionally enabled no production credential reader or writer. - `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174360 - The merged prerequisite supplies PostgreSQL migration and rollback attribution rather than this credential cutover. Label justifications: - `P2`: This is an approved storage and ownership improvement without an established urgent production incident. - `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: Shared credential tables are retired and client versions must coordinate; the rollback re-pairing tradeoff is explicitly recorded in the merged prerequisite. - `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`: The app-control endpoint now returns private credential material and depends on current UID, root, and owner-lifetime authority. - `rating: 🧂 unranked krab`: Overall readiness is 🧂 unranked krab; proof is 🧂 unranked krab and patch quality is 🦐 gold shrimp. - `status: 📣 needs proof`: The PR needs real behavior proof before ClawSweeper can clear the contributor ask. ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - Add final-effect proof for foreign UID, foreign root, and closed or replaced native owners, including closure while credential work waits. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab.
